1.detail: The Path to Hokage hit hobby stores April 28, 2006 and the first booster run sold out at most distributors, which got roughly half of what they ordered. Blister boosters were diverted to hobby stores, and mass retail (Toys R Us, Walmart, Target) got product in June. Blister and hobby packs have the same cards and insert rates.
A second, Unlimited printing of Series 1 boosters, without the First Edition mark and with minor text corrections, was due at retail in September 2006.
Series 1 booster cards carry the First Edition mark, but the starter-deck cards do not. An unmarked Set 1 card can be a starter-deck copy, not only Unlimited.

6.detail: Eternal Rivalry has 113 cards, 80 of them with art and effects never released in Japan, plus some Japanese vending-machine limited cards. Hobby street date July 27, 2007. Packs held 1 holo foil, 1 gold-stamped Rare, 2 Uncommons and 6 Commons.

8.detail: Battle of Destiny sold out at Bandai before its January 25, 2008 hobby date, and Bandai said it would not reprint. Its boosters also went into the Secrets of Masters tins (February 2008), so tin boosters are another source.

20.detail: Bandai America made alternate-art rainbow foil versions of 20 Ninja from Tales of the Gallant Sage, 20 copies of each (400 total), randomly inserted in boosters and blister packs.
